title: Lesson 20. Events
description: addEventListener, events, the e object, delegation, preventDefault

learn.intro: Hi! Lesson 20 — **events**. A real site reacts to clicks, typing and hovering. Let's go!

slides.text: Before we changed elements by hand. But a site must react to the user's actions — that is an **event**.
A button is clicked — the text changes:
Breakdown: on which element — `button`; which event — `"click"`; what to do — the function inside.

check.prompt: What goes into addEventListener as the second argument?
check.explain: The first is the event, the second is the function.

sections.title: Common events and the e object

slides.text:
`click` — a mouse click
`input` — every change of a field
`submit` — form sending
`mouseover` / `mouseout` — the cursor entered / left

check.prompt: Match the event and when it fires

slides.text: There are many elements — attaching a handler to each is awkward, and new ones won't get it. The fix: **one handler on the parent** and a check through `e.target`. Like one guard at the entrance instead of a guard at every door.
When a form is submitted the page reloads. To cancel — `e.preventDefault()`:

check.prompt: What is the idea of delegation?
options: One handler on the parent instead of many
check.explain: The parent catches clicks on its children.

slides.text: An input and an «Add» button: a click creates a new `li` with the text from the field.
Homework: clicking an item removes it. Use delegation on the whole list.

check.prompt: Which method creates a new element?

questions.prompt: An event is the site's reaction to a user action.
questions.explain: A click, typing, hovering — all events.

options: One handler also works for new elements
To make the page load longer

questions.prompt: What will clicking an item do?
With delegation the handler is attached to the parent.
questions.explain: The parent catches clicks on its children.

questions.prompt: What happens WITHOUT preventDefault on form submit?
Which method cancels the default action? (no brackets and no e.)

options: Adds the li element to the list

questions.prompt: Why input.value = "" after adding a task?
options: To clear the field for the next task
questions.explain: The field is empty again and ready for input.
